name: Terra
desc: The one who does not know what she is. Half of something, and nobody will say which half. Moves like she is waiting to be told she is allowed.
provenance_note: MEASURED before this card was written, studio/_tools/known_char_probe.py at seed 9090 on animagine-xl-4.0, evidence at studio/samples/cast/known_terra_probe.jpg. The bare name 'terra branford' returns a BLONDE IN A WHITE HOOD - not her. The danbooru form 'terra branford (final fantasy vi)' reaches the right palette and silhouette and reliably adds an orb held in both hands, which is a noun the tag genuinely carries. But the description-only control lands nearly as close, so the tag is thin and the name is doing less work than its fame suggests. She therefore gets the SAME full build as an invented character - sheet, turnaround, trained LoRA - and the name is used only to seed a better starting portrait. See craft/KNOWN_CHARACTERS.md.
source_note: A character from a published game, so this card records where she comes from. Rendering fan work is ordinary - the danbooru corpus this checkpoint learned from is largely built on it. DISTRIBUTING a finished film built on her is a different question from making one, and it is the author's call to make deliberately rather than by accident. This is not the same as the four blocked voice packs in studio/voices/, which clone real people; those are a likeness question and stay blocked.

note: BUILT AS A TEST OF THE KNOWN-CHARACTER PATH, 2026-08-04. The identity vocabulary is deliberately CONCRETE - green hair, red ribbon, red cape, gold dress, red boots, pointed ears - because the model renders nouns, not adjectives, and an identity resting on 'ethereal' or 'haunted' does not survive a single re-render. The danbooru tag leads the tag string because tag order is load-bearing on the anime path: earlier and more specific wins. The orb the tag likes to add is deliberately NOT in the wear vocabulary - it is a prop, and a prop welded to a character turns up in every shot whether the scene wants it or not, which is the same failure the styles library recorded when a style named after an object put that object in the subject's hands. | REMOVED 'pointed ears' after looking at the first sheet: it produced full elf ears, which is not her design - she reads human in FF6 and the Esper form is a separate thing. A wrong noun is worse here than a missing one because the LoRA would train it in permanently, and every later render would carry ears the card never wanted. Caught at the sheet stage, which is the cheap place to catch it.

costume_note: FOUR COSTUMES, each with the SAME FIVE DAMAGE LEVELS, because damage is orthogonal to wardrobe - armour dents the way a dress tears, and folding the two together would lose the ladder that already works. `wear_tags` is unchanged and still means the default costume, so every existing card and film is untouched. Every level names objects and their state rather than a mood, because the model renders nouns: 'battle-worn' renders as nothing, 'one pauldron dented, dried blood on the gauntlet' renders.
lora_verdict: MEASURED by looking at studio/samples/cast/terra_lora_check.jpg - two places the 16-view training set never contained, four columns, one seed. THE TRAINING BEAT THE TAG DECISIVELY. Column 1, the danbooru tag with no LoRA, puts her tiny and dark in the far distance with the face unreadable in both places. Column 2 at 0.5 frames her properly, holds green hair, red ribbon, red cape, gold patterned dress and red boots, and reads as one person across both. Column 4 is the one that decides whether she is a cast member or a prompt trick: with the danbooru name STRIPPED OUT of the prompt entirely she still comes back as Terra. The weights carry her, not the tag, so she can be put in any scene like VIRO or NIKA. Column 3 at 0.85 confirms the NIKA finding on a second character - snow_road's forest collapsed to a flat beige void. 0.85 destroys the setting; 0.5 does not.
style_verdict: MEASURED, studio/samples/cast/terra_possibilities.jpg, IPAdapter 0.0 with the LoRA at 0.5 carrying identity alone. cel_anime_90s, watercolour and oil_painting land cleanly and she survives all three. TWO STYLES HIJACK THE COMPOSITION rather than just the medium: ukiyo_e put her as a small figure inside an ornamental arch and gothic_illustration shrank her to a kneeling figure in a wide hall - the same frame-building behaviour art_nouveau and illuminated_manuscript were recorded doing in the styles library. Pin the shot size in the prompt when using those.
costume_verdict: MEASURED and it exposes a real limit. court dress LANDS - green gown, different silhouette, circlet. imperial plate and field coat only PARTLY land: a pauldron and a gauntlet appear but the gold dress persists underneath. THE LoRA MEMORISED THE DEFAULT COSTUME. It was trained on 16 views of one outfit, so the outfit is encoded as part of the identity and a costume change now fights the weights that make her her. This is not a flaw in the costumes map - it is a property of how the character was trained, and it will apply to every LoRA-backed character in the project. Fixes worth trying, in order: caption the training set so wardrobe words are separable from identity words; lower the LoRA for costume-change shots; or build the turnaround across two costumes.
